features.title: A routine's model is picked from a list in its editor: Profile’s default (empty: the profile's minutes model), Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, or Other… with a field for any name; saved as the routine's one `model` value (haiku, sonnet, opus, the name typed, or empty) and reopened with the same choice
A run asks Claude Code for the routine's model: its log's first line names it ("…, model haiku"), as does the run's What it did; Profile’s default names none but the profile's own
A routine whose stored model isn't haiku, sonnet or opus (written by hand or before the list) opens with Other… picked and its name in the field, kept as it is when saved
The routine's row in the list, and its panel's AI line, show its model when one is set (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, or the name typed), nothing when it's the profile's default
Its install sheet says it shows Echo's background jobs and changes them only in its screens (`uses.echo.jobs`), and its listing gives its summary

Two tabs, Routines and System (kept as left; ⌘K opens either): every routine — the user's or Echo's own job — drawn by the same row from the one routine contract: name and schedule (model), next run (a time, "paused at night", or "On its events"), last run (state, when, how long, cost), where it sends, its last 15 runs as bars (cost, else time; a failed one red) with its 30 days' runs and cost (or "no model"); facts above each table

A system routine opens into the routine panel (sends to, when, at night, model, what; its last 30 runs in three charts — cost per run, errors (a cell a run), time against the median (slow ones amber) — then each run's state, time, model, Echo's one line and cost) and its editor (Edit): its timer fields with units, the night and the model (Default, Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) saved at once with Save; ↺ back to a default; Echo's refusal shown, the editor kept; Cancel changes nothing

The shared night in the tab's head ("Night 22:30 → 07:00"): its times clicked to edit in place, saved on leaving a field or Enter, Escape cancels; ↺ back to Echo's own when changed; Echo's jobs keep their settings when the Scheduler is removed

What Claude may do, in the routine's editor, is Echo's routines choices: Auto (picked for a new routine) or Skip all permission checks (with its warning), no Read only; saved as `tools: auto` or `skip`; the row and the panel name it ("Auto", "Skip all permission checks"), the run asks Claude Code for it (its log: "asked: auto" / "asked: skip"), and a run's page says what that run asked (Echo's `permissions.json`), not the routine's choice now

A routine of before with `tools: read` or `folder` keeps running, as Auto: its row and panel say Auto, its editor opens with Auto picked, its run asks for auto; switching it on or off changes only its `enabled:` line, and a save writes `tools: auto`

On an Echo that has plugins' offered commands (ctx.expose), Scheduler offers other plugins and Claude in Echo `routines` (id, name, schedule, on) and `runs` (reading) and `run` (run now); on an older Echo they stay its own commands
